title: Finite discrete-valuation normalization and tame inertia character
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$ and residue characteristic $p>0$. Let $L/K$ be a finite Galois field extension (finite, normal and separable) [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $B$ is a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $B$, the localization $B_{\mathfrak n}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $L$ and residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak n)$ finite over the residue field of $A$. Put $D=\{\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/K):\sigma(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak n\}$ and $I=\{\sigma\in D:\sigma\text{ acts trivially on }\kappa(\mathfrak n)\}$. If $t$ is a uniformizer of $B_{\mathfrak n}$ and $e=v_{B_{\mathfrak n}}(\pi_A)$ is the ramification index for a uniformizer $\pi_A$ of $A$, the formula $\chi(\sigma)=\overline{\sigma(t)/t}$ defines a homomorphism $\chi:I\to\mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak n))$, independent of $t$, where $\mu_e(E)=\{z\in E^\times:z^e=1\}$. Its kernel $P$ is normal in $D$ and is a finite $p$-group (a finite group whose order is a power of $p$). If $n$ is the largest divisor of $e$ prime to $p$, then $\mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak n))=\mu_n(\kappa(\mathfrak n))$ is cyclic of order $n$, and $\chi$ induces an isomorphism $I/P\cong\mu_n(\kappa(\mathfrak n))$.

source.place: Tags 09E8 (remark-finite-separable-extension: finite normalization and DVR localizations) and 09EE (lemma-galois-inertia and equation-inertia-character: p-group kernel and cyclic tame quotient)

proof.text: By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $A$ is a principal ideal domain. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] to obtain that $A$ is Noetherian and integrally closed, and [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one] to obtain $\dim A=1$. Since the finite Galois extension $L/K$ is separable, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite] gives that its integral closure $B$ is a finite $A$-module.

source.place: Tag 09E8 (remark-finite-separable-extension), finite normalization sentence; finiteness uses finite separability, not excellence

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres] to the Noetherian dimension-one domain $A$ and the finite extension $L/K$. It gives that $B$ is Dedekind and all its residue extensions over $A$ are finite. For the chosen maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, [lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr] gives that $C=B_{\mathfrak n}$ is a DVR. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], $\operatorname{Frac}(B)=L$. As $B\subseteq C\subseteq L$, taking fractions shows also $\operatorname{Frac}(C)=L$: every fraction of elements of $C$ is in $L$, and every fraction of elements of $B$ is a fraction of elements of $C$. The residue field of $C$ identifies with $B/\mathfrak n$, since every denominator outside $\mathfrak n$ has nonzero, hence invertible, image in this field; this is $\kappa(\mathfrak n)$ in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 09E8 (remark-finite-separable-extension), Dedekind domain and local DVR sentences

proof.text: The contraction $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak n\cap A$ is the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$. Indeed $B/\mathfrak n$ is a field integral over $A/\mathfrak q$ by the monic-equation definition in [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. A subring $R$ of a field $E$ over which $E$ is integral is a field: for $0\neq a\in R$, a monic equation for $a^{-1}$, multiplied by $a^{d-1}$, expresses $a^{-1}$ as an element of $R$. Thus $\mathfrak q$ is maximal and must be $\mathfrak m_A$. The formula for the maximal ideal of $C$ in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] makes $A\to C$ local. In particular $\pi_A\neq0$ belongs to $\mathfrak m_C$, so $e=v_C(\pi_A)>0$ and $\pi_A=ut^e$ for a unit $u$. Every $K$-automorphism of $L$ preserves $B$ by applying it to monic equations. If it belongs to $D$, it extends to $C$ by $b/s\mapsto\sigma(b)/\sigma(s)$, preserves $\mathfrak m_C$, and induces an automorphism of $k'=\kappa(\mathfrak n)$. Hence $I$ is the kernel of the residue-action homomorphism of $D$ and is normal in $D$.

source.place: Tag 09E8 and Tag 09EE (lemma-galois-inertia), passage to C and its group action; the contraction argument is written out

proof.text: Let $n$ be the largest divisor of $e$ prime to $p$. The hypotheses of [lem-exc-dvr-inertia-order-prime-part] now hold for $A,L,B,\mathfrak n,C$: $C$ is a DVR by Step 2 and $A\to C$ is local by Step 3. Consequently $|I|=np^b$ for some $b\geq0$. This retains the possible purely inseparable part of the residue extension; no assertion $|I|=e$ is used.

source.place: Tag 09EE (lemma-galois-inertia), first proof paragraph, the prime-to-p order calculation

proof.text: For $\sigma\in I$, write $\sigma(t)=a_\sigma t$ with $a_\sigma\in C^\times$, since it is another uniformizer. Applying $\sigma$ to $\pi_A=ut^e$ and cancelling $t^e$ gives $u=\sigma(u)a_\sigma^e$. Since $\sigma$ fixes $k'$, reduction gives $\bar a_\sigma^e=1$. Define $\chi(\sigma)=\bar a_\sigma\in\mu_e(k')$. For $\sigma,\tau\in I$, $a_{\sigma\tau}=\sigma(a_\tau)a_\sigma$; reducing gives $\chi(\sigma\tau)=\chi(\sigma)\chi(\tau)$. If $t'=wt$ with $w\in C^\times$, then $\sigma(t')/t'=(\sigma(w)/w)a_\sigma$, whose reduction is unchanged. This proves both the homomorphism assertion and independence of $t$.

source.place: Tag 09EE (lemma-galois-inertia), second proof paragraph and equation-inertia-character

proof.text: Let $P=\ker\chi$. For $\delta\in D$ and $\sigma\in P$, normality of $I$ gives $\delta\sigma\delta^{-1}\in I$. The element $t'=\delta^{-1}(t)$ is a uniformizer of $C$. The residue of $(\delta\sigma\delta^{-1})(t)/t$ is $\bar\delta(\overline{\sigma(t')/t'})=\bar\delta(\chi(\sigma))=1$, using the uniformizer independence from Step 5. Thus $\delta\sigma\delta^{-1}\in P$, so $P$ is normal in $D$.

source.place: Tag 09EE (lemma-galois-inertia), proof of normality; explicit conjugation computation in place of the associated-graded description

proof.text: For $\sigma\in P$ and every $i\geq0$, $(\sigma-1)(t^iC)\subseteq t^{i+1}C$. To check this on $t^i a$, use $\sigma(a)\equiv a\pmod t$ and $\sigma(t)/t\equiv1\pmod t$ to obtain $\sigma(t^ia)-t^ia=t^i((\sigma(t)/t)^i\sigma(a)-a)\in t^{i+1}C$. Now let $\sigma\neq1$ have order $m$, finite because $I$ is finite by Step 4. There is $c\in C$ not fixed by $\sigma$, since otherwise it fixes $\operatorname{Frac}(C)=L$. For $d=\sigma(c)-c\neq0$, the discrete valuation gives $d\in t^iC\setminus t^{i+1}C$ for a finite integer $i\geq1$. The preceding congruence implies $\sigma^j(d)\equiv d\pmod{t^{i+1}}$ for all $j\geq0$. Telescoping gives $0=\sigma^m(c)-c=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\sigma^j(d)\equiv m d\pmod{t^{i+1}}$. Write $d=t^i a$ with $a$ a unit. Dividing the last containment by $t^i$ and reducing modulo $t$ gives $m\bar a=0$ in the characteristic-$p$ field $k'$, hence $p\mid m$.

source.place: Tag 09EE (lemma-galois-inertia), telescoping proof of the p-group assertion, with the valuation and congruences explicit

proof.text: The group $P$ is finite as a subgroup of the finite group $I$ from Step 4. If a prime $q$ divides $|P|$, [lem-exc-finite-group-cauchy] supplies $\sigma\in P$ of order exactly $q$. It is nonidentity because $q>1$, so Step 7 gives $p\mid q$, whence $q=p$. Thus every prime divisor of the positive integer $|P|$ is $p$. Integer prime factorization gives $|P|=p^a$ for some $a\geq0$, including $a=0$ if $P=1$. This proves the finite p-group assertion.

source.place: Tag 09EE (lemma-galois-inertia), final sentence of the p-group argument, making its Cauchy-theorem input explicit

proof.text: Write $e=np^s$. Since $p$ is prime, the intermediate binomial coefficients $\binom{p}{j}$ vanish in characteristic $p$, so $(X^n-1)^p=X^{np}-1$. Iterating $s$ times gives $X^e-1=(X^n-1)^{p^s}$, which shows that $\mu_e(k')=\mu_n(k')$: a power of an element of a field is zero only if that element is zero. By [lem-exc-field-roots-cyclic-bound], $\mu_n(k')$ is finite cyclic with at most $n$ elements. If $z$ is a generator and its order is $r$, the equality $z^n=1$ and division of $n$ by $r$ show $r\mid n$. The cosets of a subgroup partition a finite group into sets of equal subgroup size, so its order divides the group order. Consequently the orders of $\mu_n(k')$ and of every subgroup, including $\operatorname{im}\chi$, divide $n$ and are prime to $p$.

source.place: Tag 09HW (section-roots-of-1), opening root bound, cyclicity and final characteristic-p observation; the application is the roots-of-unity paragraph of more-algebra.tex Tag 09EE (lemma-galois-inertia)

proof.text: Put $h=|\operatorname{im}\chi|$. Each fibre of $\chi:I\to\operatorname{im}\chi$ is a coset of $P$, so $|I|=|P|h$. By Steps 4 and 8, $np^b=p^a h$, and $h$ is prime to $p$ by Step 9. Taking prime-to-$p$ parts gives $h=n$. But $\operatorname{im}\chi\subseteq\mu_n(k')$ and $|\mu_n(k')|\leq n$, so equality of the finite sets follows, and $|\mu_n(k')|=n$. Finally the map on cosets $I/P\to\mu_n(k')$, $\sigma P\mapsto\chi(\sigma)$, is well-defined and multiplicative. It is surjective by the equality of the image just proved; if two values coincide, their quotient belongs to $\ker\chi=P$, so the cosets coincide. This is the asserted isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Expanded finite normalization using existing PID, normalization and Dedekind-localization nodes. Proved the tame character, its uniformizer independence, kernel normality, the valuation telescoping estimate, the Cauchy p-group implication and surjectivity by explicit finite-order comparison. Added one strictly auxiliary statement-only numerical inertia-order lemma allowing imperfect residue fields and two exact Mathlib leaves (Cauchy and cyclic roots with cardinality bound). No mathematical statement was changed; existing notion references and the meaning of finite p-group were made explicit. Second reading removed the worker-authored tool-use decision for maintainer review, corrected the roots-of-unity source file and expanded the Frobenius identity by binomial coefficients.

The item is a non-key descendant in the inherited sk-prop-a1-kummer unit; no unit or chapter record is changed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NH-919a6d11f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full item and all three new nodes against Stacks more-algebra 09E8 and 09EE (both proofs read; 09EA, 09EB and 09ED also read) and fields 09HS, 09HW and 09HX. The item's assertion is unchanged from the base copy; only definition references were added. Its hypotheses match the source exactly: an arbitrary DVR and finite Galois L/K, with no henselian, excellent or perfect-residue assumption. Steps 1-10 hold. Step 3 shows that n meets A in the maximal ideal and that I is normal in D. Steps 5 and 6 prove that χ is a homomorphism independent of t and that ker χ is normal by conjugating the uniformizer. Steps 7 and 8 carry out the valuation telescoping and the Cauchy argument, so |P| is a power of p. Steps 9 and 10 show μ_e = μ_n, then compare prime-to-p parts to get |im χ| = n and the isomorphism. lem-exc-dvr-inertia-order-prime-part is true (|D| = ef, the surjection onto Aut of the normal residue extension, and |Aut| = f_s give |I| = e·p^c). It is strictly smaller than the item and not a duplicate; its unsplit status is justified because Mathlib's inertia order theorems require a perfect residue field. The Cauchy leaf (exists_prime_orderOf_dvd_card', Perm/Cycle/Type.lean:544) and the roots leaf (Finite at 245, rootsOfUnity.isCyclic at 249, card_rootsOfUnity at 252 of RootsOfUnity/Basic.lean, with NeZero k at 208) match the pinned Mathlib. A rg search of the DAG and blueprint_refs searches found no duplicates. Blueprint from/via/same_as are correct and no SGA source is used. Edge cases checked: L = K; tame Kummer; Artin–Schreier; and the imperfect-residue example after 09EE, where e = 1 and |I| = 2. One off-unit dependency: step 2 uses lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres (unit sk-thm-curveestimate). I accept it as tool_uses: it is a generic result that the integral closure is Dedekind, as 09E8 itself uses, and no node of sk-prop-a1-kummer gives it. No fixes.
